messages:
maya: Heads-up 10AM run vs MedStream POC produced repeating tail spikes during a steady ramp. Need quick triage + clear cost estimate for a dedicated short burst. Sharing observations and config.

trent: What's the test harness and what numbers did you capture?

maya: We used a k6 script (US-WEST) hitting /v1/chat/stream. Script ramped from 50 -> 400 RPS over 20m. Prompt size ~400 tokens. Rough results: avg 130ms, p95 280ms, p99 850ms, periodic spikes to 1.5s for 10-15s windows roughly every 3 minutes. No retries in client. Errors low (~0.1%).

julie: Which model + runtime flags? Hosted or Dedicated?

maya: Hosted tenant; model=redwood-7b-chat, quant=medium. Client didn't enable batching or KV caching. Using simple curl-based driver for initial baseline.

trent: Likely causes: transient queueing when token generation bursts align + worker scaling jitter. Also, if they require per-request KMS/HSM calls, that will add per-request latency. Two experiments to run:
1) re-run pinned to a 2x-GPU Dedicated pool to eliminate noisy neighbor and cold-start jitter.
2) enable continuous batching (max size 24, max latency 25ms) + KV prefix cache to smooth peaks.

maya: Here's the call we used:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<~400-token-prompt>"}],"max_tokens":64}'
```

julie: For Dedicated POC burst pricing: we can offer a 4-hour pool at list-equivalent pricing; fin-ops to confirm exact hourly rate per A10 equiv and any one-off setup.

fin-ops: I can provide a ballpark now: 2x A10 equiv for 4 hours => ~ $YY/hr * 2 * 4 = approx $ZZ (finals after finance check). For Private + HSM integration there will be setup fees; I'll detail in follow-up.

maya: MedStream security flagged HSM per-request signing requirement. They worry KMS roundtrips will kill p99. Any guidance?

trent: If your path does an online KMS call per request, expect an extra 20-80ms depending on network and HSM. Best practice is envelope encryption: cache DEKs locally and only hit the HSM on key rotation or DEK unwrap. That reduces steady-state overhead to <10ms. If compliance demands real-time HSM ops, expect to budget ~100-150ms to p99.

maya: Can devops-bot simulate a 50ms per-request KMS delay so we can quantify impact?

devops-bot: Scheduled synthetic: medstream-sim-361024-a, config=200 VUs, 12m, inject latency=50ms at KMS hop. Results will be posted to #eng-runtime when done. :satellite:

julie: Also note MedStream requires IP allowlist + SCIM. For a short Dedicated POC we can provide temporary static egress IPs and a SCIM trial connector.

trent: Tech run checklist for the next attempt:
- pin to Dedicated (2x A10)
- enable SDK batching + streaming endpoint
- enable KV prefix cache
- reduce prompt to 256 tokens as a follow-up if latency still high
- collect runtime metrics (GPU util, queue lengths, GC pauses)

maya: Timeline: they want an updated report + pricing by EOD tomorrow. Can we hit that?

fin-ops: I'll get a conservative number by EOD and a final after finance review in 24h.

trent: I'll trigger the Dedicated soak once pool is up. @devops-bot please spin up temp-pool-3610 (2x A10) for 6h.

devops-bot: temp-pool-3610 request accepted. ETA ~20m. Run windows will be posted.

maya: Assigning owners: triage & runs (trent), pricing & finance (fin-ops), security questionnaire + SOC2 + HSM writeup (julie). I'll be the point to relay results to MedStream.

trent: Quick tip 5: set k6 thresholds to abort if p99 > 700ms so we don't waste cycles, and enable extended logging only on failing windows. Also hook the runtime probe to export histograms.

maya: Thanks team. If we can show p99 <300ms with envelope pattern, sales can move forward without Private. If not, we'll need to map Private deployment timeline and costs. :thumbsup:
